m1-waive-produced-by-and-mismatch.title: PART A -- fix waive() produced_by and add report-only authority_mismatch
m1-waive-produced-by-and-mismatch.imperative: In waive() (scripts/checklist_engine.py): (1) change the evidence entry's produced_by from the literal 'human' to the passed authority. (2) Read policy.get('authority') (currently never read) and compare it, case/whitespace-normalized, against the passed authority. On mismatch, set authority_mismatch: true and expected_authority on BOTH the new evidence entry's payload and c['waived']; waive() must NOT refuse or block on a mismatch -- same return string shape as before. On match or when policy.get('authority') is absent, add no new field (absence stays meaningful, not False/None). Write/extend unit tests in tests/test_checklist_engine.py covering: produced_by echoes authority; mismatch sets both fields report-only; match sets neither; absent policy.authority sets neither. Run `pytest tests/test_checklist_engine.py -k waive -q`.

m2-dispatch-claim-release-wiring.title: PART B (claim + release branches) -- wire force-claim/force-release into override_ledger from dispatch() only
m2-dispatch-claim-release-wiring.imperative: In dispatch()'s claim arm: after claim(...) returns successfully, read the just-written cl['engine_session'] -- if force was passed AND previous_session_id is non-null (genuine takeover), call _append_override_entry(cl, 'force-claim', verb='claim', session_id=..., previous_session_id=..., takeover_reason=...). A no-op --force (nothing to take over) must NOT append. In dispatch()'s early release arm: capture the owning session_id from cl.get('engine_session') BEFORE calling release(...) (release mutates status but leaves session_id in place). Compute whether to append (force was passed AND caller's session_id differs from the captured owner) and, if so, call _append_override_entry(cl, 'force-release', ...) inline BEFORE the existing return release(...) statement -- do NOT convert the early return into a fall-through (that would newly route release's output through the shared bottom logic including the archived-path banner, an unintended behavior change). Write tests: force-claim over a genuine takeover appends; no-op --force claim does not; force-release by a non-owner appends before the early return; a force-release against an archived-path spine gets ZERO archived-banner decoration in its output (regression test for the early-return care). Both append calls must go through _append_override_entry, never write cl['override_ledger'] directly, and must NOT appear inside claim()/release()'s own function bodies.

m3-dispatch-waive-wiring-and-parity.title: PART B (generic/waive branch) -- record every successful waive from dispatch(), plus the duplicate-lookup-parity test
m3-dispatch-waive-wiring-and-parity.imperative: In dispatch()'s generic verb branch (the _run_verb call): when v == 'waive' and _run_verb returns successfully, read the condition's now-set c['waived'] marker (dispatch already has cl and the target ids from args) and append kind='waive' via _append_override_entry with the marker's authority/reason/forced/authority_mismatch/expected_authority fields plus task/cond/evidence. Record EVERY successful waive, not only forced/mismatched ones. The condition lookup dispatch performs for this read must use the SAME lookup path waive() itself exercises (same which-then-fallback search over preconditions/postconditions) -- write a test with a condition id that exists in BOTH preconditions and postconditions with different override_policy, proving `which` is threaded through correctly to both dispatch's re-lookup and waive()'s own lookup (a divergence test). Also write the direct-call-vs-dispatch-call chokepoint test: one test drives waive/claim --force/release --force through checklist_engine.dispatch() (the CLI path via main()/dispatch()) and asserts override_ledger entries land; a companion test calls waive()/claim()/release() directly as library functions and asserts override_ledger is UNCHANGED.
